messages.subject: Transect Capture History Verify Message
parts:
I am receiving the message 'XY coordinates not on transect' with the entire list of my detections when verifying my capture history (transect detector). I have visually ensured that all of my detections are on transects, have increased my tolerance to thousands of meters to see what happens, and have tried with another person's data and all attempts have given me the same message. Is this message standard? The models are still able to run, but I have run into some difficulty in successfully snipping the transect data into a 'count' detector and I'm wondering if the issues are related. I would appreciate any insight! 

Katherine Kurth

I also have an unrelated question. I have gone through the documentation, help files, and groups and can't find a solution that has worked yet. Is there a way to get individual covariate specific densities without using the conditional likelihood? I want to model habitat covariates on D but would like the density ratio of an individual covariate. The individual covariate is genetic pool (4 categories). I know I can't use the conditional likelihood with habitat covariates on density, and hcov isn't ideal for more than two levels. I have also tried modeling genetics as a group with CL=FALSE, but can't find a 'derived' function equivalent for the full likelihood. Is there a way to get the individual covariate density ratio with the full likelihood? I really appreciate your help! 

Katherine

messages.subject: Re: Transect Capture History Verify Message
parts:
Yes, the genetic group is a permanent attribute for each individual. I was able to get group density predictions using predict(), but there have been some odd results described below. 

 

#Null model results in 61 individuals (61 EN 61 RN), which is similar to other models I have run

fl <- secr.fit(mch, CL = FALSE, model = list(D~1, g0~1, sigma~1), details = list(sigma = 920.836), mask = extractedmask, detectfn = 'HHN')

region.N(ffl)

 

#Null model just identifying that groups are present results in 15 individuals (15 EN 31 RN). This is underestimating the number of individuals from what I’ve observed on the landscape

flg <- secr.fit(fch, CL = FALSE, groups = 'Genetics', model = list(D~1, g0~1, sigma~1), details = list(sigma = 920.836), mask = extractedmask, detectfn = 'HHN')

region.N(fflg)

 

#Model placing genetics as an individual covariate on lambda results in 40 individuals (40 EN 55 RN)

flgg <- secr.fit(fch, CL = FALSE, groups = 'Genetics', model = list(D~1, g0~g, sigma~1), details = list(sigma = 920.836), mask = extractedmask, detectfn = 'HHN')

region.N(fflgg)

 

#Trying a couple of different ways to specify all levels get me the same results each time. The density estimates multiplied by the hectares result in a prediction of 40 individuals for each of the four genetic pools represented by this sex, which doesn’t sum to the overall abundance estimate for the mask. I would think the density estimates for each group should be quite different and add to 40 individuals rather than 164 individuals since 40 was the abundance estimate. This is confusing to me.

predict(fflgg)


secr.make.newdata(fflgg, all.levels = TRUE)

predict(fflgg)


predict(fflgg, all.levels = TRUE)

 

This is my male data, but the same pattern is occurring with my female data as well. Any model that even mentions "groups" estimates about half of the abundance estimate given by other models and each genetic pool accounts for the entirety of the density estimate, not matching the abundance estimate calculated by the same model. I am unsure what I'm doing to get such varying and unmatched results. Have you seen this occur before?
